texts.preamble: Pramod Kumar vs . Samarth Gupta & Ors. on 27 July, 2022 :1: In The Court Sh. Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi Mact No.979/17 Fir no.172/17 Ps Lodhi Colony U/s 279/337/338 Ipc Pramod Kumar Vs. Samarth Gupta & Ors. Cnr No Dlse01-009403-2017 Pramod Kumar S/o Late Sh. Chandrapal Singh R/o H. No. 251, Block no.30 Trilokpuri, New Delhi. ...Claimant Versus 1. Samarth Singh S/o Sh. Gideon Singh ............Driver/Respondent no. 2. Gideon Singh S/o Late Sh. V. K. Singh Both R/o: Gayatri Appartment Building 2520, Main Jagadumba Road, Tughlakabad Extension, New Delhi. ............Owner/Respondent no. 2 3. M/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company. 7th Floor, Dlf Towers, 15 Shivaji Marg, New Delhi. .........Insurance Company/Respondent no. 3 Mact No.979/17 Pramod Kumar Vs. Samarth Gupta & Ors. Page No. 1 of 24 Date of accident : 25.11.2017
texts.facts: Compensation case regarding injury to Pramod Kumar Yadav aged about 42 years, with 28 % permanent disability in relation to his right upper limb AWARD 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. Brief facts of the case are that on 25.11.2017, petitioner was going by his scooty bearing no. DL 7SBX 6634 from Meherchand Market, Lodhi Colony to Barapurla. When he reached near Gate no.4, Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium at about 03.30 PM, a car bearing no. DL 8CAK 3263 came from wrong side. The driver of the offending vehicle was driving the car on wrong side and in very rash and negligent manner. He (petitioner) drove his scooty towards left but the driver turned his car into his right side and hit his scooty from the one side. Due to this impact, he fell down on the road and got injuries. 3. The driver of the offending vehicle brought him to the Moolchand Hospital in his car where his MLC bearing no. 5342 dated 25.11.2017 was prepared. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 31.12.2019 noticing 28% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right upper limb. 4. An FIR bearing No.431/18 u/s 279/337/338 IPC PS Lodhi Colony, New Delhi was registered in this case. Page No. 2 of 24 5. In response to DAR, despite opportunities available, respondent No.1 and respondent no.2 did not file their reply. In fact, such R-1 / Respondent no.1 and 2 did not contested the present petition which is clear from record. 6. In response to claim petition, respondent no.3/ Insurance Company filed legal offer which was not acceptable to the petitioner. Hence, this matter proceeded further on merit. 7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 04.06.2018 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: 1. 8. Petitioner Pramod Kumar, filed his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/1. He relied upon original bank passbook/ bank statement as Ex.PW1/A, copy of ID issued by LIC as Ex.PW1/B, copy of bank statement showing transaction dated 17.11.2017 as Ex.PW1/C, DAR as Ex.PW1/D, original discharge summary as Ex.PW1/E and Ex.PW1/F and original medical bills as Ex.PW1/G. Pramod Kumar vs . Samarth Gupta & Ors. on 27 July, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124879473/ 2 9. Such PW-1/ Victim/ Injured / Petitioner was cross examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company/ respondent no.3. During cross examination, he deposed that he was plying the scooty no. DL 7SBX 6634 which belongs to his friend on the date of accident. He has not supplied the RC and Insurance Policy of the scooty. He is working as Insurance Agent with LIC since about August 2017. He has filed copy of ID issued on 02.11.2017 by LIC. He has filed proof MACT No.979/17 Pramod Kumar Vs. Samarth Gupta & Ors. Page No. 3 of 24 of income from LIC as an agent. He admitted that he received Rs. 80,000/- (rupees eighty thousands) in connected criminal case. 10. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 11. No evidence was led on behalf of respondents. Further, they also filed written arguments. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). 15.2. The nature of injuries are grievous and petitioner suffered 28% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right upper limb. The petitioner has Rs. 2,10,000/- deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit that at the time of accident, he was working as insurance agent with LIC. It is further claimed that he got his first commission through bank dated 17.11.2017 of Rs. 10,523/= through bank and copy of bank statement is Ex.PW1/C. It is further deposed that, he was working as driver with one Mr. Jason Ashok Kothari. It is further claimed that he was getting a salary of Rs. 40,520/= along with overtime as his last salary. It is further claimed that due to such claim, he could not work for about 5 months. Considering the nature of injury and disability report and the evidence on record, it is held that income shown from LIC agency is not a regular income as only one month incentive is shown. Further, PW-1/injured in his examination-in-chief deposed that his last salary with overtime was Rs.40,520/- dated 07.11.2017. Further, he placed on record copy of his bank statement receiving regular payment ranging from Rs.30,000/- to such Rs. 40,520/- during the period of June, 2017 to November, 2017. As such, his average salary at the time of accident is taken as Rs.35,000/- p.m. (iii) Loss of amenities of life : The Rs.50,000/- petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and suffered 28% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right upper limb.
texts.arguments: 15.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). In Cholamandlam Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD-Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet u/s 279/304 A IPC are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. In view MACT No.979/17 Pramod Kumar Vs. Samarth Gupta & Ors. Page No. 13 of 24 of judgment of Raj Kumar(supra) ,it can be noted that in the present case petitioner suffered 28% physical impairment in relation to his right upper limb. 3.Further in such case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar, the Hon'ble Supreme Court laid down a three step approach to decide compensation for the injured persons who have suffered permanent disability and same are as under: i) Tribunal should see as to what the injured can do inspite of permanent disability and what the injured cannot do: 32. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which MACT No.979/17 Pramod Kumar Vs. Samarth Gupta & Ors. Page No. 18 of 24 it is demanded and paid. Further, MACT No.979/17 Pramod Kumar Vs. Samarth Gupta & Ors. Page No. 20 of 24 in the considered view of this Tribunal, the purpose of such Award is to compensate the petitioner for the financial loss already sustained that is to reimburse the same as well as to ensure that his future earning is augmented, in the same manner in which he would have otherwise earned.
